answer: In a tundra quarry market, agents sell certified marble and basalt samples. Each order receives a random identifier after the seller commits a collateral-backed offer. Independent labs are chosen only afterward and compare blinded samples against hidden controls. One identifier earns at most one payment, regardless of aliases; conflicting signed reports trigger a dispute and bond loss. An attacker must fund extra bonds and produce distinct tested deliveries for extra rewards, so multiplying accounts cannot cheaply multiply influence.
